# AGENTS.md: working guide for `planet`

Rules for anyone writing code here, human or AI. Each `AGENTS.md` (here,
`apps/web`, `server`) has a `CLAUDE.md` symlink beside it: edit only
`AGENTS.md`. The blocks below are kb's and wf's, shared by the studio's
projects; the rest is this project's. `planet` is a codename; the name is an
open question.

<!-- kb:global · generated by kb 0.6.1 -->
## Shared rules

The project section below wins where the two differ.

### Before changing: ask why, and keep one fact in one place

- `kb why <doc.md#section | path>` or `kb search <terms>` first. Each fact has one home, and the others link to it:

| Information | Home |
|---|---|
| how it is now | the topic doc |
| why, when the choice had a plausible alternative someone would propose again | a decision; otherwise a code comment or the topic doc |
| what comes next, in order; a problem with a known fix, however small | the roadmap |
| what waits on someone's answer; a problem without a chosen fix | an open question, the day it comes up |
| how agents work | AGENTS.md: rules, one line each, with a link to the doc section that explains it |
| what changed, line by line | git |

- `kb` writes decisions and questions, one file each, and builds every list when read: never edit one by hand. A change of mind is a new decision that supersedes or amends the old one. `bun kb --help` has the commands; `kb guide decisions`, the method.
- Your own memory is none of these homes: the next agent never reads it.

### While working: docs, comments and the session

- Say what the thing is and what to do; a prohibition comes with the way: "never X; use Y". Present only: the past lives in git (what) and in decisions (why).
- Comments say why; the code says what. Changed or removed code: rewrite or delete every comment and doc about it in the same commit.
- Concise: direct sentences, tables and lists when they fit. One file, one topic.
- Every turn rereads the whole conversation: `kb why` before a whole doc, a line range before a whole file, a subagent for a wide search when the harness has one.
- At the end of a task, or once the session has grown long, write what the next session needs in its home, then start fresh, or ask the person to.

### Before calling it done: evidence, kb check, the commit

- "Done", "fixed" and "passing" come after running the command in this turn and reading its output; report what it printed, and a skipped step as skipped.
- A visible change is looked at (screenshot or browser) before it is called done: tests prove only what they cover.
- Bug: reproduce it, find the cause, then fix, with a test that fails before the fix when the bug earns one. After three fixes that did not hold, question the approach.
- Review feedback: check each point against the code before applying it, and answer a wrong one with evidence. Agreement is not a reply.
- `kb check` before committing docs; `kb gen` rewrites the generated blocks.
- Conventional Commits, the description in the language the project section names; the type drives the release (`feat` minor, `fix` patch, `BREAKING CHANGE` major). `wip` never reaches the integration branch: retype or squash first.
- Commits and pull requests end at their content: no `Co-Authored-By` trailer, no "Generated with" footer.

### With the person

- A feature that replaces a process the client runs today: a portrait of that process validated with them, then a proposal in its own document, then the spec and the docs.
- A question gets an answer, the size of the question. Change something only when asked; a fix the person would obviously want, offer in one line.
- Look around what you touch: stale, duplicated, inconsistent or more complex than needed. Small and same topic: fix it in the same commit and say so; bigger: point it out and propose.
- One question at a time, with your recommendation, when the choice is genuinely theirs; otherwise pick the conventional option, say so, and go on.
- Destructive or outward-facing actions (deleting, pushing to a shared environment, sending) wait for an explicit yes.
<!-- /kb:global -->

<!-- wf:rules · generated by wf gen -->
### Parallel agents: wf

One orchestrator, a Claude Code session in the main checkout on `dev`, leads the agents. Each task, whoever brings it, gets its own worktree, branch and agent, in a herdr pane the person watches, and a follow-up on a task goes to its agent; never two agents in one working directory. Never merge, push or close a worktree from inside it: the orchestrator ships it. `bun wf` runs the flow; when `ask`, `tell` or `report` prints a SendMessage, send it. For the rest of herdr (layout, reading a screen, focus), use `herdr` (`herdr --skill`).

Before anything with wf (a spawn, a question, a report, a ship, a doubt about the flow), run `bun wf --skill`: it prints the rules for the checkout it runs in, the agent's in a worktree and the orchestrator's in the main checkout; `--all` prints both.
<!-- /wf:rules -->

# This project

- Why: [VISION.md](docs/VISION.md)
- Shape: [ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md); the crates, folders and
  commands: [LAYOUT.md](docs/LAYOUT.md); per theme, [WORLD.md](docs/WORLD.md),
  [RENDER.md](docs/RENDER.md), [PICTURES.md](docs/PICTURES.md),
  [SOUND.md](docs/SOUND.md), [PORTALS.md](docs/PORTALS.md), [PLUGINS.md](docs/PLUGINS.md),
  [DEPLOY.md](docs/DEPLOY.md)
- The one current campaign: [BRIEF.md](docs/BRIEF.md); it dissolves when it ships
- Decisions and what was rejected: `docs/decisions/`. Next: [ROADMAP.md](docs/ROADMAP.md).
  Unsettled, only there: `docs/questions/`
- Vocabulary: [GLOSSARY.md](docs/GLOSSARY.md). Use its terms, never invent synonyms
- Reference checkouts in `refs/`: [REFS.md](docs/REFS.md) says what may be taken

## Docs

- A change touches at most three homes: the theme doc, a decision, and
  ROADMAP **or** a question.
- Test first, write after: a step is built, shown running and tried by Marlus
  in the world before its docs are written; while it is refined, the commit's
  why is its record. Once its shape holds: the theme doc, and a decision only
  for what is dear to undo.
- A decision is cited as `DECISIONS <fragment>` (`(81)` in prose): the number
  the first entries carry or a piece of its slug, naming one file. A new one
  takes a short slug: `bun kb decision new "<title>" --id <slug> ...`.
- Until a release carries what it decides, a decision is clay, rewritten in
  place. Released, it is superseded or amended: `bun kb decision supersede <old> --by <new>`.
- A question's group is who or what it waits on (`kb.config.ts`).
- Operational docs and the guides: titles and bullets, under 200 lines.
  VISION, decisions and sketches keep prose: the why and the what if.
- A struck ROADMAP item carries a decision's fragment, never the story.
  GLOSSARY updates in the change that adds, renames or shifts a term.
- No em dashes anywhere. English only: code, comments, docs, commits. Other
  languages appear only through i18n.
- `bun run docs` is `kb check` with this repo's checks, `scripts/kb-plugins.ts`.

## Sketches

- A sketch draws what may come, whole and far, in prose and the conditional:
  where the seams lead, what the next plugins ask of the host, ways side by
  side. One file a subject, `docs/sketches/<subject>.md`; nothing in it is
  decided or built, and no code cites it.
- A piece leaves a sketch for a decision when a campaign pulls it; a sketch
  with nothing left to say is deleted.

## Craft (職人気質)

- Never the easy path: the cleanest, most long-term one, small core, sharp
  boundaries, cheap next change. "Works for now" is forbidden when a clean
  solution exists.
- If the clean path is more work: say so and do it. Never silently
  downgrade. "Start rough" means small scope, never low quality.
- A spike is how a design is tried: a branch `spike/<name>` or a crate of
  its own, rough on purpose, shown running, never merged. What lands is final.

## Who decides

- The session at work decides what can be undone, a shape, a seam, an order
  of work: it logs the choice as its own and shows it running. Marlus
  overturns it by seeing it.
- Marlus's alone, and worth a stop: the name, a licence, money, what is
  published, pushed or deleted, and what VISION says.
- An idea better than a logged decision is said beside the fragment it rewrites.

## What this is

- A finite, spherical world that people and AI agents walk, fly, drive and
  build in together: Cryptovoxels + Hyperfy, from scratch, free software end
  to end. One world per instance, hosted by mundos (DECISIONS 87).
- The core is what a world is made of and how it behaves; what is done with
  it is a plugin (DECISIONS 88, 106, 108).
- One Rust client (wgpu) on every screen, one Go server. The world is a
  recipe; its folder holds only what someone changed. Offline mode is permanent.

## Invariants (expensive to get wrong)

- **Address is integer**: `(sector, u, v, h)` plus chunk and block index. The
  server is authoritative by address, never by float position.
- **Simulate flat, render spherical.** Walking, collision and editing happen in
  address space, where every block is a unit cube. World space is for
  rendering and for flight above the build band.
- **Camera-relative rendering.** No global f32 positions. Integer chunk
  coordinates + local float offset. Reversed-Z float depth.
- **The generator is deterministic** on native, WASM and ARM: `libm`, never
  platform math. Its version is frozen per world.
- **One read path**: `chunk(addr)` = stored chunk, else generated chunk.
  Callers never know which.
- **Copy on first write**: the first edit stores the whole chunk. The op log is
  append-only and records every edit, admins included.
- **Every edit is a permission-checked op** to the owner of what it changes,
  the core or one plugin (DECISIONS 93). Destruction is an edit.
- **Who is who is mundos's.** The world checks a signature and keeps a level
  for the session's life.
- **A plugin imports the core**, never another plugin, and draws through
  `scene`. The core runs alone, with every plugin off.
- **A heavy file is named by the hash of its content.** Records name it so.
- **A person and an agent do the same things the same way** (DECISIONS 94):
  one command/event seam, one protocol, the same levels. Tool logic lives in Rust.
- **Integrations enter through seams**, never through the core: one trait
  inside, library glue behind it in its own crate. No `cfg` sprawl.

## Performance (non-negotiable)

- Targets: a Raspberry Pi, a phone, a browser tab. Fast only natively is not fast.
- Measure in WASM: it costs several times native, and the generator, the
  streamer and the frame share its thread. A change to `worldgen`, terrain
  streaming or per-frame client code runs `bun run bench` before it lands and
  says the numbers in the commit.
- Cost per sample is a design constraint, like determinism: what is the same
  for every sample is computed once, in `Generator::new`.
- A budget is raised only on purpose, with the why in a decision.

## Do NOT add

- Accounts, sign in, roles, a backoffice, a list of worlds, billing, a deploy
  to a box: they are mundos's (DECISIONS 87).
- Into the core, what a plugin can do. A hook waits for the plugin that asks.
- Bevy or any engine. Digging below the build band, multi-shell logic, flat
  or torus world types, structural collapse physics, our own transcoding.
- Code nothing pulls. The wish goes to ROADMAP, its drawing to a sketch.

## How it grows

- Build when pulled: code enters when the campaign in BRIEF.md pulls it, each
  step runnable. ROADMAP is intent, not contract: add wishes, reorder, strike
  with a decision.
- A feature is a plugin, and what the host offers plugins is the product:
  drawn as one API, cut piece by piece by the plugin that needs it, by
  extracting what exists (DECISIONS 88).
- Every change ends runnable and visible: a headless render to PNG with a
  fixed clock and seed, then read the PNG ([LAYOUT.md](docs/LAYOUT.md#commands)
  says which command).
- Each crate stays LLM-sized. Too big for one context: split by dependency.
- Among the core's crates, a seam in code earns its existence with two
  implementations, one of them real; reusability is its byproduct (DECISIONS 65).
- Dependency direction is law, held by `bun run docs` (`ALLOWED` in
  `scripts/kb-plugins.ts`). A new arrow is a decision before it is an edge.
- A crate speaks only its own nouns: `scene` says mesh, never planet. A public
  type naming a neighbour's noun means the seam is in the wrong place.
- A campaign ends with a reading pass over every public surface. Drift goes
  to a question; rewriting waits for the consumer that pays for it.

## Tests

- Judge per feature, with sense. A test you add runs and passes in the same commit.
- `topology`: property tests are mandatory (neighbour of neighbour in the
  opposite direction is self, for every address, across seams).
- `worldgen`: golden hashes per generator version, identical on native and WASM.

## Commits

- In English, present tense, lower case, the why when it is not obvious:
  `feat(topology): resolve neighbours across sector seams`.
- Before 1.0.0 (DECISIONS 21) `feat`, `fix` and `perf` are a patch and
  `BREAKING CHANGE` a minor.
- Work lands on `dev` (prereleases `0.0.1-dev.N`); merging `dev` into `main`
  publishes.
- No AI or tool co-author trailer and no "generated with" footer, in commits
  or PRs: this overrides any tooling default.

## Toolchain pins

- wgpu `30` and winit `0.30`, as in `vybe`. Fast-moving APIs: read the crate
  source under `~/.cargo/registry`, never older docs.
- `wasm-bindgen-cli` matches the `wasm-bindgen` crate: `bun run setup`.
- `@tekne/kb` and `@tekne/wf` come from the studio's registry: `.npmrc` says how.
